method: Option C then B, decided by the owner on 23 September 2026. C: candidate terms are taken only from the field where an agency is asked to name its vendor, never from the field naming its own authorised system. B: every remaining term that actually appears in the narrative text was then inspected in context and classified by hand.
why_the_source_field_matters: A term earns its place from the field where an agency names a supplier. The field naming an agency's own authorised system contains government system names, and replacing one of those with [product] would state something false: it would present a public system as a commercial product.

removed_after_context_inspection.category: government or agency system named in the vendor field by the agency that operates it
reasons: A federal procurement system. The commercial tools named alongside it remain on the list separately.
An agency research chatbot, described in the data as a model for an intramural community.
The same chatbot under different casing.
An agency-built assistant, entered in the vendor field by the agency that built it.

removed_after_context_inspection.category: ordinary words and technical terms that reached the vendor field
reasons: The ordinary word for a connection or link, as in an agency nexus.
A statistical method, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator.
The ordinary expression for round-the-clock availability.

added_back_by_hand.why: Option C drops the field that also carried some genuine commercial products. Those were recovered rather than accepted as a cost of the change.
categories: a commercial camera and evidence supplier

classification_of_firing_terms.note: Every term that now fires was named by an agency in the vendor field and confirmed in context as a commercial product or supplier.
